summary: Discovery focused on Suncrest's security and compliance requirements for hosting PHI-adjacent inference workloads. Main concerns: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML with IdP, fine-grained RBAC, audit logs & retention, envelope encryption/KMS, and data residency. Team is leaning toward Redwood Dedicated or Private due to isolation and compliance; next step is exchange of SOC2/ISO docs and a technical deep-dive to validate VPC/networking and KMS integration.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-17
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Alex Mercer (Redwood AE), Priya Sharma (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (CSM) -- Dana Lopez (CISO, Suncrest), Mark Huang (VP Eng), Leah Patel (DevOps), Omar Reed (Security Eng)

[00:00] Alex Mercer: Hey everyone, uh, thanks for joining. I'm Alex with Redwood Inference, and this is Priya, our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Dana Lopez: Hi, thanks. We'll try to be crisp, we have about 40 minutes.
[00:11] Priya Sharma: Great, we'll run through security posture, answer questions, and capture next steps.
[00:18] Mark Huang: High level - Suncrest is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private. Primary must-haves: SOC2 Type II, SSO/SAML through Okta, RBAC with least privilege, full audit logs, envelope encryption w/ KMS, and a data retention policy for model inputs/outputs. Also, we handle regulated data, not full PHI but PHI-adjacent.
[00:36] Alex Mercer: Got it. Quick question on compliance - you said SOC2 Type II and ISO?
[00:40] Dana Lopez: Yes, ISO 27001 would be nice to see. And for any private deployment we may need an on-prem option or at least a VPC with customer-managed keys.
[00:49] Priya Sharma: That's common. Redwood offers SOC2 and we have customers with ISO through our infra partners - we'll share certs. For encryption we support customer-managed KMS for Dedicated and Private; hosted supports provider-managed keys but we do envelope encryption and can integrate with customer KMS in VPC mode.
[01:08] Omar Reed: When you say integrate with customer KMS, is that an HSM-backed key or do you support bring-your-own-key where we hold the root?
[01:15] Priya Sharma: For Dedicated and Private yes, you can bring keys via AWS KMS with a customer master key; HSM-backed is possible via partner integrations, we can surface a diagram. For hosted API, we default to provider-managed but have options for enterprise tenants.
[01:27] Leah Patel: Network - we need private subnets, no public egress except through approved NAT, and control plane telemetry can't cross our VPC. Is control plane traffic encrypted and can we restrict egress?
[01:39] Alex Mercer: Control plane uses TLS and mTLS for runtime. For Redwood Private the control plane is in your network or a private peering; for Dedicated we offer VPC peering options and egress controls. We can provide a runbook showing control plane vs data plane separation.
[01:50] Mark Huang: Audit logging - do you provide immutable audit logs, user-level actions, model access, prompt-level traceability? Retention policies?
[01:58] Priya Sharma: We capture detailed audit events: API calls, model version deploys, user auth events, and admin actions. Logs can be streamed to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) or to your S3 with lifecycle rules. Retention is configurable per account; for regulated workloads we commonly set 7 years but it's configurable.
[02:14] Dana Lopez: Can you redact or avoid storing prompts that contain PII? Our legal says avoid retention of raw inputs unless necessary.
[02:21] Priya Sharma: We support token-level redaction and optional prompt stripping before storage. For Dedicated/Private deployments the default is you control retention - Redwood can be configured to not persist inputs in logs. Hosted customers can enable prompt obfuscation.
[02:34] Omar Reed: SSO - Okta. We need SCIM provisioning and SAML 2.0 support with MFA enforcement and role mappings. How granular is RBAC? Can we enforce per-model, per-route permissions?
[02:46] Alex Mercer: Yes, we integrate with SAML/OAuth and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC supports roles and policies; you can map IdP groups to Redwood roles. In Dedicated/Private you get more granular roles: per-model, per-route, and per-environment permissions. Hosted has role granularity but some advanced controls are limited to enterprise tenants.
[03:04] Mark Huang: Do you support attribute-based access control, e.g., enforce data residency tags so only certain models in region A can be accessed by certain users?
[03:11] Priya Sharma: We have tag-based routing and can bind policies to model tags and regions. For strict residency we recommend Dedicated in-region or Private on-prem.
[03:20] Leah Patel: About encryption-in-transit and at-rest - we need TLS1.2+, perfect forward secrecy, and at-rest with AES-256 and keys rotated quarterly. Is rotation automatic and can we trigger it?
[03:33] Priya Sharma: TLS 1.2+ with PFS is standard. For KMS-backed keys you can auto-rotate or control rotation windows; for customer-managed keys rotation is handled by your KMS; Redwood can kick key rotation events and re-encrypt as needed in Dedicated/Private.
[03:45] Dana Lopez: Incident response - can you share your IR playbook and SLAs on notification? We require 24/7 notification for sev1 within one hour and a post-incident report within 7 days.
[03:57] Alex Mercer: We comply with enterprise SLAs; we can share our IR playbook and support matrix. For enterprise customers we do 1-hour notif for critical incidents and formal RCA within a week.
[04:08] Omar Reed: Pen testing & vuln scans - Do you accept customer scoping requests and share results? Is there an authorized testing window?
[04:14] Priya Sharma: Yes, we have a program for authorized pentests on Dedicated and Private; hosted is subject to our security team approval - we can provide a schedule and scope. We also run third-party scans regularly and have bug-bounty engagements.
[04:28] Mark Huang: A couple tradeoffs - latency and cost. If we go Hosted, we'll get faster time to market but less control over data residency and keys. Dedicated gives isolation and custom KMS but higher cost; Private on-prem is the most isolated but more ops. Thoughts?
[04:41] Alex Mercer: That aligns with how most customers think. Redwood Dedicated is often a good middle ground for regulated companies: reserved capacity, VPC peering, and customer-managed KMS. Private is used when regulators require on-prem or air-gapped. We can run a proof-of-concept on Dedicated to show economics.
[04:56] Leah Patel: For POC/benchmarks - we want a run where we push our typical request mix and measure p95 latency and cost per 1k tokens. Can you provision a dedicated pool for a week?
[05:05] Priya Sharma: Yes, we can provision a short-lived dedicated pool for benchmark runs. We'll need details on model size, sequence lengths, concurrency. We'll also show quantization/throughput options.
[05:15] Dana Lopez: About logs and evidence for auditors - do you provide tamper-evident logs or chain-of-custody?
[05:21] Priya Sharma: We have append-only storage options and can hash log bundles for later verification. For high-assurance customers we can integrate with your archival process.
[05:31] Mark Huang: Any red flags on integration? We run K8s on EKS, use Okta, Splunk for logs, and have a centralized KMS. We want minimal firewall changes and prefer PrivateLink if possible.
[05:42] Alex Mercer: We support PrivateLink and VPC peering, and we can provide limited set of egress IPs to allowlist. Integration with EKS is straightforward with our SDKs and agent-based injector for inference calls if you prefer.
[05:56] Omar Reed: One more - model auditability. We need to log model version, weights fingerprint, and config used per request to reproduce in audits.
[06:04] Priya Sharma: We capture model metadata, git-hash-like model fingerprints, and config at inference time. We can surface that in logs and in per-request tracing.
[06:14] Dana Lopez: Great. I think our legal/security wants to see SOC2, ISO, and data processing addendum. Also an export showing how long you retain inputs & outputs by default.
[06:23] Alex Mercer: We'll send SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001 cert, DPA template, and a retention config doc.
[06:29] Jordan Lee: I'll coordinate scheduling the deep dive for the week of 4/27.
[06:33] Mark Huang: Sounds good. Also can you share pricing for Dedicated and a ballpark for Private on-prem?
[06:39] Alex Mercer: We'll include high-level pricing ranges in the follow-up; detailed quoting requires usage profile.
[06:44] Dana Lopez: Ok thanks, that's all from us.
[06:47] Priya Sharma: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with artifacts.

[End of recording]
notes: Customer emphasized regulatory requirements; prefer Dedicated for POC. Legal/security requested SOC2/ISO, DPA, and retention export. Technical next-step is a benchmark run on Dedicated with KMS integration and VPC networking check.
